name: Cha Cha Coconuts
blurb: The Circle's open-air tropical bar and grill, right next door to Columbia. Frozen drinks, fish sandwiches, burgers and a breezy patio that sits at the busiest corner of St. Armands.
tip: Grab a sidewalk table late afternoon: it is the best seat on the Circle for watching the whole island walk by.

geocode.display: Cha Cha Coconuts, 417, Saint Armands Circle, Saint Armand's Circle, Lido Key, Sa

name: Cilantro Grill
blurb: Small, quick Latin grill tucked into the Gold quadrant next to Cha Cha Coconuts. Tacos, burritos and bowls when you want something fast and fresh between shops.
tip: The easy answer when half the group wants a sit-down lunch and the other half wants tacos in ten minutes.

geocode.display: Saint Armands Circle, Saint Armand's Circle, Lido Key, Sarasota, Sarasota County

name: Crab & Fin
good_for: Dinner, date night, seafood, early-bird dining
blurb: Serving the Circle since 1978: fresh fish, crab, oysters and a long wine list on a shaded sidewalk patio with live music most evenings. The classic St. Armands seafood dinner.
tip: The early dining menu (4:45 to 5:45) is one of the better values on the Circle, and it gets you a patio table before the evening rush.

geocode.display: Crab & Fin Restaurant, 420, Saint Armands Circle, Saint Armand's Circle, Lido Ke

name: Daiquiri Deck
good_for: Frozen drinks, happy hour, oysters, groups
blurb: The Lido branch of the island frozen-drink institution: a wall of daiquiri machines, an oyster bar, and an open-air deck on the Pink quadrant that stays busy from lunch until late.
tip: Oyster happy hour plus a frozen drink is the local move before walking over to Lido Beach for sunset.

name: Lynches Pub & Grub
address: 19 N Blvd of the Presidents, Sarasota, FL 34236
food_style: Irish pub, burgers, fish and chips
good_for: Beer, whiskey, lunch, watching a game
blurb: A proper Irish pub a few steps off the Circle: 16 beers on tap, more than 100 Irish whiskeys, pub food and the Circle's most loyal local crowd. The Irish gift shop is next door.
tip: Where the Circle's shopkeepers eat lunch. Sit at the bar if you want the real neighborhood gossip.

geocode.display: Lynches Pub & Grub, 19, Boulevard of the Presidents, Saint Armand's Circle, Lido

name: Nonno Umberto Italian Seafood & Steakhouse
address: 22 S Blvd of the Presidents, Sarasota, FL 34236
good_for: Dinner, date night, celebrations, homemade pasta
blurb: The Salustri family's return to the Circle: Le Colonne closed after the 2024 storms and reopened in January 2026 as Nonno Umberto, with homemade pasta, fresh seafood and prime steaks in the same South Boulevard spot.
tip: Ask for the family's story. This is the comeback restaurant of the Circle, and the regulars treat it that way.

name: Tommy Bahama Restaurant & Bar
blurb: The island-lifestyle brand's restaurant and bar, now in the former Shore space on the Gold quadrant with the retail store beside it. Coconut shrimp, fresh fish and rum drinks in a polished tropical room.
tip: Reliable for a group with mixed tastes and a dependable reservation when the Circle is slammed in season.

geocode.display: Shore St Armands Circle, 465, John Ringling Boulevard, Saint Armand's Circle, Li

name: Blue Dolphin Cafe
blurb: The Circle's breakfast spot: omelets, pancakes, benedicts and lunch plates from a kitchen staffed by Culinary Institute grads. Small, busy and beloved by Lido condo owners.
tip: Weekend brunch lines form by 9. Come at 8 or after 11 and you will walk right in.

geocode.display: Blue Dolphin Cafe, 470, John Ringling Boulevard, Saint Armand's Circle, Lido Key

name: Blu Kouzina
address: 25 N Blvd of the Presidents, Sarasota, FL 34236
blurb: Authentic Greek on North Boulevard: grilled whole fish, meze, lamb and olive oil from the owners' own groves in a crisp white-and-blue room.
tip: Order a spread of meze for the table and let the kitchen pace it. The grilled octopus is the dish people come back for.

name: 15 South by Napulè
address: 15 S Blvd of the Presidents, Sarasota, FL 34236
good_for: Pizza, dinner, late drinks, families downstairs
blurb: Wood-fired Neapolitan pizza from the Napulè team: a family dining room downstairs and a bar upstairs that keeps going after the shops close.
tip: Downstairs for the kids, upstairs for a nightcap. One of the few places on the Circle with a real evening bar scene.

name: Rico's Pizzeria
good_for: Pizza by the slice, quick lunch, takeout, families
blurb: The Sarasota pizza family's Circle location: big New York slices, calzones and pasta you can walk out with and eat on a park bench.
tip: The cheapest good meal on the Circle. Grab slices and sit in the center park under the statues.

name: Ephesus Mediterranean Delights
address: 27 N Blvd of the Presidents, Sarasota, FL 34236
food_style: Turkish and Mediterranean cafe, baklava, Turkish coffee
blurb: A small Turkish cafe and sweets shop on North Boulevard: baklava, Turkish delight, Turkish coffee and tea, plus light Mediterranean plates.
tip: Boxed baklava from here is a better hostess gift than anything in the boutiques.

name: Pinchers (opening late 2026)
blurb: The Gulf Coast crab-and-shrimp chain is building out 8,000-plus square feet in the former Tommy Bahama space at 300 John Ringling, targeting an October 2026 opening. The biggest new dining room the Circle has had in years.
tip: Check before you walk over: opening timelines on the Circle slip. Once open, expect it to absorb the big-group dinners.

name: Ben & Jerry's
blurb: The scoop shop on the Purple quadrant, next to Venezia. Lines form after dinner; the park benches across the street are the dining room.
tip: Grandkid currency, same as Big Olaf on Siesta.

name: Big Olaf Creamery (St. Armands)
blurb: The Circle's Big Olaf, now scooping Yoder's Southern Creamery small-batch ice cream in a waffle cone. Tucked on North Washington behind the Pink quadrant, so the line is shorter than the Siesta one.
tip: A cone and a lap of the Circle at dusk is the whole St. Armands evening for a lot of our clients.

name: Kilwins Chocolates & Ice Cream
blurb: Fudge made on the marble slab in the window, hand-dipped chocolates and ice cream on the Purple quadrant. You will smell it before you see it.
tip: The fudge travels; buy it on the way back to the car, not on the way in.

geocode.display: Kilwins, 312, John Ringling Boulevard, Saint Armand's Circle, Lido Key, Sarasota

name: River Street Sweets
blurb: The Savannah candy maker's Circle shop: warm pralines, glazed pecans, taffy and ice cream a few doors from Kilwins.
tip: Free praline samples at the door. Yes, really.

name: Settimi's Gelato
blurb: Small-batch Italian gelato and espresso on the Pink quadrant, the grown-up alternative to the ice-cream lines across the Circle.
tip: Affogato and a slow walk around the park after dinner at Columbia or Venezia.

geocode.display: Settimi's Gelato, 367, Saint Armands Circle, Saint Armand's Circle, Lido Key, Sa

name: I Love Candy & Ice Cream
blurb: Bulk candy, novelty sweets and scoops on the Aqua quadrant next to Alvin's Island. The kids will find it before you do.
tip: Pair with the beach-shop run: Alvin's for the boogie board, here for the sugar.

geocode.display: 440, John Ringling Boulevard, Saint Armand's Circle, Lido Key, Sarasota, Sarasot

name: Le Colonne
address: S Blvd of the Presidents, Sarasota, FL 34236
blurb: Classic Italian on South Boulevard of the Presidents, a few doors off the Circle: pasta, veal and a proper wine list in a white-tablecloth room.
tip: The old-school choice for a long dinner after the shops close.
